key_insight: A stacking machine-learning model using pre-operative clinical features can predict which Mohs micrographic surgery cases will need 13 or more sections.
clinical_relevance: This could help teams plan operative time, allocate resources, and counsel patients before surgery.
method: Analyzed 408 consecutive Mohs procedures with 16 pre-operative clinical variables.
Compared 30 machine-learning models, including ensemble, boosting, neural network, SVM, and traditional classifiers.
Used 5-fold stratified cross-validation, an independent test set, and SHAP to identify key predictors.
evidence_signal: The stacking ensemble achieved the best performance, with cross-validation AUC 0.891 and test AUC 0.884, and 70.7% of predictions were high-confidence.
watch_item: External validation across multiple centers is still needed before routine clinical use, since performance may vary by population and practice pattern.
paper_title: Development and Validation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting 13 or More Sections in Mohs Micrographic Surgery
